{{Quote|Kadann may be a dwarf, but I suggest that you don't underestimate him, my Lordship.|Grand Moff Hissa to Trioculus|<ref name="LCJ">''[[The Lost City of the Jedi]]''</ref>}}
'''Nanism''' was a medical or genetic condition that resulted in an abnormally short adult height. An individual affected by nanism was referred to as a '''dwarf'''. The term "dwarf" was also used inaccurately to describe [[Species/Legends|species]] the average stature of which was naturally short, or miniature breeds within a given species.

In the [[galactic community]], people with nanism sometimes encountered discrimination, especially in cultures that valued tallness as well as powerful build like the [[Sanyassan/Legends|Sanyassan]] society.

==Characteristics==
{{Quote|Amnesty? Imperial amnesty is about as valuable as a Wookiee dwarf with no hair.|[[Thaddeus Ross]], making a politically incorrect comparison|<ref name="TFE" />}}
[[File:Yavid.jpg|thumb|left|The noble Yavid was constantly belittled by his peers on [[Sanyassa IV]].]]
Nanism occurred when an individual was of unusually diminutive stature by reference to their [[Species/Legends|species's]] average, due to a developmental or congenital disease.<ref name="dbYavid" /> It was the polar opposite of [[giantism]], an abnormal increase in physical size and stature.<ref name="DP">[[Darth Plagueis (novel)|''Darth Plagueis'']]</ref>
[[Human/Legends|Humans]],<ref name="DSS" /> [[Wookiee/Legends|Wookiees]]<ref name="TFE" /> and [[Sanyassan/Legends|Sanyassans]]<ref name="dbYavid" /> were among the varieties of [[Species/Legends|species]] that could develop this condition. The [[Near-Human]] [[Bimm/Legends|Bimms]] from the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Bimmisaari/Legends|Bimmisaari]], who stood from 1.0 to 1.5 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] for adults of both [[Gender/Legends|sexes]],<ref name="UAA">''[[Ultimate Alien Anthology]]''</ref> could easily pass as Human dwarfs.<ref name="END">{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/member/insideronline/88/indexp2.html|text=''Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties''|int=Evil Never Dies: The Sith Dynasties}}</ref>

Nanism was sometimes a cause of psychological difficulties resulting from social intolerance. The Sanyassan [[Noble/Legends|noble]] [[Yavid]] initially had some trouble in his [[Homeworld/Legends|homeworld's]] hierarchy due to his congenital diminutive size. In reaction to being constantly trodden upon, Yavid had to develop an explosive personality that could gain him a respected place among his peers.<ref name="dbYavid" />

On at least one occasion, the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] [[Warlord/Legends|warlord]] [[Trioculus]] mocked little people with disdain and scorn, although the [[Grand Moff/Legends|Grand Moff]] [[Bertroff Hissa|Hissa]] advised him not to underestimate his adversaries according to their size.<ref name="LCJ" /> Ironically, Trioculus himself was afflicted with a more exotic deformity, as he was a three-[[Eye/Legends|eyed]] [[mutant]].<ref name="GDV">''[[The Glove of Darth Vader]]''</ref>

The term "dwarf" was often mistakenly used as an adjective to describe smaller breeds within a species, like the [[Dwarf bantha/Legends|dwarf bantha]]<ref name="WoSW">''[[The Wildlife of Star Wars: A Field Guide]]''</ref> and the [[dwarf varactyl]],<ref name="RebScum">{{Rebelscum|url=SSC16crumb.asp|text=Salacious B. Crumb (Creature Pack)}}</ref> or even in reference to species in which the small stature was the norm&mdash;such as the porcine [[Ugnaught/Legends|Ugnaughts]] or the industrious [[Nord]]s.<ref name="TWOY">{{JournalCite|2|The Way of the Yrashu}}</ref> The verb "to dwarf" was also used, meaning "to make appear smaller or insignificant". For example, the [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] [[Music/Legends|minstrel]] [[Gobi Glie/Legends|Gobi Glie]] once stated: "But our foes have no legends; that's where we dwarf them."<ref name="TBCS">''[[The Clone Wars: The Ballad of Cham Syndulla]]''</ref>

==History==
{{Quote|That black-bearded dwarf has proven to be even more of a scoundrel than Zorba the Hutt.|Grand Moff Hissa on the pseudo-Kadann|<ref name="PDS">[[Prophets of the Dark Side (novel)|''Prophets of the Dark Side'']]</ref>}}
[[File:Pseudo-Kadann-AGSWU2.jpg|thumb|right|A Bimm impostor posing as Kadann, a Human dwarf]]
In the last decades of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]], the one-meter tall [[Actor/Legends|actor]] [[Palleus Chuff]] played mostly villainous scheming dwarfs, although he became famous for his outstanding portrayal of the diminutive [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Yoda/Legends|Yoda]] in his self-written play ''[[Jedi!]]''.<ref name="YDR">''[[Yoda: Dark Rendezvous]]''</ref>

The Human [[Kadann]], a former [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] who turned evil and became the [[Supreme Prophet]] of the [[Dark side of the Force/Legends|dark side]], was born with nanism,<ref name="DSS" /> with an adult height of only 1.3 meters.<ref name="poly">{{PolyhedronCite|103|Prophets of the Dark Side: Villains for the Star Wars: New Republic Campaign, Part One}}</ref> After the [[Battle of Endor/Legends|Battle of Endor]], the former [[Director of Imperial Intelligence]] [[Cronal]] set up a "[[Church of the Dark Side]]" with a clergy of false Prophets, including the Near-Human Bimm [[Rajah Ubooki]] to impersonate the real Kadann.<ref name="END" /> Believing the impostor to be the genuine Kadann, both the Imperial and the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebels]] referred to the Bimm agent as "the [[Color/Legends|black]]-bearded dwarf".<ref name="PDS" />

Among his many assumed shapes, the [[Changeling/Legends|shapeshifter]] [[Rokur Gepta]] would sometimes take the appearance of what others described as "a malignant dwarf."<ref name="sharu">''[[Lando Calrissian and the Mindharp of Sharu]]''</ref>

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|I was an 11-year-old boy at school, and my grandmother happened to hear a radio commercial on the London radio station. They were putting out a call for short people to be in this new ''Star Wars'' movie.|Warwick Davis|<ref name="Empire of Dreams">''[[Empire of Dreams: The Story of the Star Wars Trilogy]]''</ref>}}
In real life, nanism (also known as "dwarfism" or "short stature") can take many forms, some of which are hereditary. The Little People of America (LPA) define nanism as an adult height of 148 cm (4 feet 10 inches) or less.<ref name="LPA">{{WebCite|url=http://www.lpaonline.org/faq-#Definition|text=Little People of America&mdash;FAQ|archivedate=20120814121325}}</ref>

[[File:Weazel2.jpg|thumb|left|150px|Actor Warwick Davis in ''Star Wars Episode I''.]]
''Star Wars'' creator [[George Lucas]] has been working with little people on a regular basis during his career as a movie director. At one stage during pre-production of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], Lucas planned for [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]], along with his [[Owen Lars/Legends|uncle]] and [[Beru Whitesun Lars/Legends|aunt]], to be played by little people.<ref name="SWI127">{{InsiderCite|127|Mon Mothma's 5 Facts}}</ref> In [[1977]], Lucas eventually hired [[Kenny Baker]] to play the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] in ''A New Hope''.<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref> In [[1983]], for [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']], Lucas recruited several actors with short stature to portray the [[Ewok/Legends|Ewoks]] from [[Endor/Legends|Endor]], including [[Warwick Davis]], [[Kevin Thompson]] and [[Jack Purvis]].<ref name="ROTJ">{{Film|VI}}</ref> Davis went on to play the [[Thorn Drumheller|title character]] in [[Willow (film)|''Willow'']], another Lucas movie that was released in [[1988]]. This movie was notable for employing more little people than any production in many years, and was widely praised for employing Warwick Davis as the lead.<ref name="LFCM4">[[The Lucasfilm Fan Club Magazine 4|''The Lucasfilm Fan Club Magazine'' 4]]</ref>

A diminutive character called [[Weazel/Legends|Weazel]] appeared in the [[May]] [[1999]] film [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'']], in which he was portrayed by Warwick Davis. Although he looks like a Human dwarf, Weazel's species has never been revealed, and he could belong to a diminutive species like the Bimms. However, Weazel's entry in ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' states that he was "short and stocky" for his species.<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|III|323|Weazel}}</ref>

According to the ambiguously [[canon]] article ''[[Prophets of the Dark Side: Villains for the Star Wars: New Republic Campaign, Part One]]'', the real Prophet Kadann measured 1.3 meters, while his apprentice [[Jedgar]] stood at 2.3 meters in height.<ref name="POLY">{{PolyhedronCite|103|Prophets of the Dark Side: Villains for the Star Wars: New Republic Campaign, Part One}}</ref> However, a picture of the two prophets together was shown in ''[[The Dark Side Sourcebook]]'', and the height difference does not seem to be that significant.<ref name="DSS" />
